note: Hash-commitment over a LIVE append-only OMP session (status=cutoff) — NOT a byte-level frozen copy. content_sha256 + record_count are a cryptographic commitment pinned at pinned_at over the first record_count records of the EXTERNAL file at `path`, which remains mutable (the session kept appending after capture). Re-verification — recompute sha256 over the first record_count lines of `path` and compare; a mismatch proves drift. The raw bytes are deliberately NOT committed (content_bytes is large and sensitivity=sensitive session content), so this enables drift DETECTION, not byte RECOVERY — if `path` is deleted or rewritten the bytes are unrecoverable. 'Immutable' here means the commitment value, not a stored artifact. content_sha256/record_count are point-in-time / live-at-capture, not a final total; models/ended_at are carried from the source inventory row, not re-derived over post-snapshot records.
freeze_semantics: verifiable-prefix commitment (OMP session JSONL is append-only): re-verify at any time by `head -c <content_bytes> <path> | sha256sum` and comparing to content_sha256 — MATCH proves the frozen prefix is immutable; MISMATCH means the source was rewritten/compacted and the commitment is VOID (bytes unrecoverable, since raw bytes are deliberately NOT committed — large + sensitive session content). This establishes immutability by an executable check, not a stored copy.
